implementation_notes: Bunny mirrors the AMQP property: create an exclusive server-named queue, publish with reply_to: queue.name and correlation_id:, and the worker republishes to properties.reply_to with the same correlation id — the shape of the RabbitMQ RPC tutorial. Ruby's in-process equivalent is a Thread::Queue handed to the worker thread, but anything crossing processes should use the broker header, and clients that cannot afford a queue per request should use the amq.rabbitmq.reply-to pseudo queue.
idiom_name: Bunny reply_to / correlation_id on an exclusive callback queue
code_sketch:
queue = channel.queue('', exclusive: true)
exchange = channel.default_exchange
exchange.publish(message, routing_key: 'rpc_queue',
                 correlation_id: correlation_id, reply_to: queue.name)
queue.subscribe { |_info, props, payload| resolve(payload) if props.correlation_id == correlation_id }

# server
exchange.publish(result.to_s, routing_key: properties.reply_to,
                 correlation_id: properties.correlation_id)
pitfalls: Bunny shares a channel across threads by default; publishing a reply from a subscription callback while another thread publishes needs separate channels.
An exclusive reply queue is deleted when the connection closes, so a client crash converts in-flight replies into silent drops.
A publish to a reply queue that no longer exists is discarded unless the mandatory flag and a return handler are enabled — turn them on while developing.
